title: Morris USF Lab Protocol Demo
author: Lauren Segers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5gbg3sn

steps.title: Pre-surgical Preparation
steps.instruction: Administer initial medications to the adult cats (3.1–5.8 kg) to prepare for surgery.

substeps.instruction: Inject atropine (0.54 mg/kg i.m.) to reduce airway mucus secretion.
Administer Dexamethasone infusion: initial bolus of 2.0 mg/kg followed by 4.5 mg kg-1 h-1 i.v. to minimize brain stem swelling and prevent hypotension.

steps.title: Anesthesia Induction and Maintenance
steps.instruction: Induce and maintain anesthesia using isoflurane mixed with medical grade air (21% O2-Balance N2-Airgas).

substeps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 5.0% isoflurane.
Maintain anesthesia with 1.0–3.0% isoflurane until decerebration.

steps.title: Surgical Access and Monitoring Setup
steps.instruction: Establish surgical access and monitoring lines.

substeps.instruction: Intubate the trachea following induction.
Place catheters in the femoral arteries and veins for drug/fluid administration and arterial blood pressure monitoring.
Perform a bilateral thoracotomy (pneumothorax) in some animals.

steps.title: Physiological Maintenance
steps.instruction: Monitor and maintain arterial blood parameters and blood pressure.

substeps.instruction: Periodically analyze arterial blood for PO2, PCO2, pH, and HCO3- concentrations.
Infuse 8.4% sodium bicarbonate solution to correct metabolic acidosis as needed.

Maintain mean blood pressure of at least 75 mmHg using intravenous administration of 6% Hetastarch or 5% Dextran in half-normal saline (0.45%), 0.04–0.1% dopamine, and/or 0.075–0.3 mg/ml phenylephrine in lactated Ringer solution.

steps.title: Decerebration Procedure
steps.instruction: Perform decerebration and expose the brainstem.

substeps.instruction: Ligate both external carotid arteries caudal to the lingual artery branch to reduce bleeding.
Administer neuromuscular blocker (vecuronium bromide or pancuronium bromide) immediately prior to transection: initial bolus 0.1 mg/kg and continuous infusion 0.2 mg kg-1 h-1 i.v.
Perform an occipital craniotomy, midcollicular transection, and suction decerebration.
Expose the brainstem and remove the pia mater.
Insert tungsten microelectrodes to measure neuron extracellular potentials.
Gradually reduce isoflurane concentration to zero following decerebration.

steps.title: Nerve Isolation and Recording Setup
steps.instruction: Isolate target nerves and set up recording electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Isolate and desheathe the right hypoglossal (XII), left phrenic (Phr), left lumbar iliohypogastric (Lum), and right vagus (X) nerves (or right recurrent laryngeal nerve [RLN] instead of X in some cases).
Place XII, Lum, and X/RLN nerves in coiled or hooked bipolar silver electrodes; cover with mineral oil and petroleum jelly, then wrap in parafilm.
Place Phr nerve in a pool of mineral oil in a neck pocket, section it, and record in coiled or hooked bipolar silver electrodes.
Amplify, full-wave rectify, low-pass filter, and RC integrate (τ = 200–500 ms) all nerve activity.
Monitor integrated nerve activity, tracheal pressure (TP), end tidal CO2, and arterial blood pressure on a Grass polygraph and record digitally (16-bit, 25 kHz per channel).
Isolate SLNs bilaterally.
Connect each to a silver bipolar electrode.
Cover with mineral oil and petroleum jelly or a mineral oil-soaked pledget.

steps.title: Evoking Fictive Swallows
steps.instruction: Trigger fictive swallows using electrical stimulation or water boluses.

substeps.instruction: Electrical Stimulation: Stimulate SLNs (pulse duration 0.25 ms; frequency 5–20 Hz; Voltage 2.6–4.0 V, 33.3–51.5 μA; train duration 2–120 s). Identify swallows by Phr, XII, and X/RLN activity.
Water Bolus: Rapidly inject 5–25 mL of distilled water (less than 5 s) through a polyethylene tube in the mouth. Perform at least three trials with an inter-trial interval of at least 2 min.

steps.title: Ventilation Mode Implementation
steps.instruction: Apply different ventilation modes to alter PSR feedback timing.

substeps.instruction: Subject-Triggered (ST) Mode: Use the integrated phrenic signal to trigger the ventilator for lung inflation and passive deflation.
Mandatory Ventilation (MV) Mode: Set ventilator rate to 30 breaths per minute; adjust gas flow rate to maintain arterial PCO2 at 30 ± 0.5 mmHg.

steps.title: Euthanasia
steps.instruction: Administer overdose of anesthetic agents following completion of protocols.

substeps.instruction: Administer Euthasol (85 mg/kg, i.v.) or sodium thiopental (20 mg/kg, i.v.), followed by potassium chloride (i.v.).
Monitor cardiac and respiratory activities until cessation.
